description: Project Overview This is a comprehensive, interactive data dashboard I developed to visualize and analyze the budget performance of 47 counties in Kenya for the financial year 2023/24. The project transforms complex public financial data from the Office of the Controller of Budget into an accessible, interactive web application. Key Features: Interactive Map Visualization -Choropleth map with color-coded counties based on key performance metrics -Dual-layer visualization (polygon boundaries + circle markers) for flexible data exploration -Popup information windows displaying detailed county-specific data -Custom legend system adapting to different metrics Multi-Metric Analysis: The dashboard tracks six key performance indicators: -Overall absorption rate -Development absorption rate -Revenue performance -Wage bill as percentage of revenue -Pending bills (in Kshs. Billion) -Total budget allocation Comprehensive Dashboard Tabs: -Performance Analysis: Top-performing counties and budget allocation patterns -County Comparison: Side-by-side radar chart comparison of any two counties -Trend Analysis: Historical performance trends over five years -Revenue Analysis: Revenue sources breakdown and own-source revenue leaders -Efficiency Metrics: Scatter plot matrices showing absorption vs. revenue performance Interactive Controls: .Metric selector to change map coloring .Region and county filters .Year selector for trend analysis .Layer toggles for map visualization control Data export functionality (CSV) Technical Implementation Frontend Technologies Leaflet.js for interactive mapping with custom GeoJSON integration Chart.js and D3.js for all data visualizations (bar charts, doughnut charts, scatter plots, radar charts, line graphs) PapaParse for CSV data handling HTML5/CSS3 with responsive design principles Data Architecture 47 Kenyan counties with 15+ data points each GeoJSON boundary data integrated with county-level metrics Regional aggregation for comparative analysis Historical trend data spanning 5 financial years Key Insights Delivered The dashboard reveals critical patterns in Kenya's county financial management: Significant variation in budget absorption rates (64.7% to 90.8%) Heavy dependency on national government transfers (72% of revenue) Wage bill pressures exceeding legal limits in multiple counties Development expenditure lagging at only 24.4% of total spending Pending bills exceeding Kshs. 181 billion overall Impact & Value: This tool serves multiple stakeholders: -Government officials can identify underperforming counties and best practices -Citizens gain transparency into public fund utilization -Researchers access clean, visualizable financial data -Policymakers can make data-driven resource allocation decisions

projects.title: Kenya Multi-Year Diaspora Remitance Flow
projects.description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW:
The Project maps remittance flows from six world regions — North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World — into Kenya using animated curved lines on a Leaflet map. The line thickness, color, and animation speed represent the remittance amount, while tooltips and popups show exact values and distances.


KEY FEATURES:
Yearly data views	-Switch between 2022–2025 to see remittance changes over time
Region filtering-Focus on a single region’s flows
Dynamic map styling-	Line width scales with remittance value; colors by region
Animated flows-	Dashed lines with pulsing/moving effects to indicate direction and scale
Statistics panel-	Shows total remittance per region and average distance traveled
Trend analysis-	Line chart and YoY growth table with market share
Data export	-Export as GeoJSON, CSV, or plain-text analysis report
Responsive design-Works on desktop and mobile screen.
 
VALUE IT BRINGS:
1. For Policy Makers & Economists
Quickly identify which diaspora regions contribute most to Kenya’s foreign exchange.

Track year-over-year growth trends to guide foreign policy, trade agreements, or diaspora engagement programs.

Understand geographic concentration of remittances for targeted financial inclusion initiatives.

2. For Financial Institutions & Remittance Companies
Spot high-value corridors (e.g., North America, Europe) for marketing and fee reduction strategies.

Analyze market share by region to prioritize expansion or partnerships.

Use exported data for internal forecasting and reporting.

3. For Researchers 
Study spatial patterns of global migration and its economic impact.

Access a clean, reusable dataset (GeoJSON/CSV) for further analysis in GIS tools like QGIS or ArcGIS.

Understand how distance correlates with remittance volume (though not causal, it’s visualized).

4. For Data Storytellers & Journalists
Embed the interactive map in articles or reports about Kenya’s economy.

Use the trend charts to visually communicate growth stories (e.g., “Middle East remittances grew 8% in 2024”).

5. Technical Value
Demonstrates integration of Leaflet + Turf.js for geodesic line calculation and spatial analysis.

Shows real-time filtering, animation toggling, and data persistence without a backend.

Serves as a template for any origin-destination flow mapping project (trade, migration, internet traffic, etc.).



TECHNOLOGY:
Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (vanilla)

Mapping: Leaflet.js + CartoDB basemap

Geospatial math: Turf.js (distance, midpoint, bounding box, geodesic interpolation)

Charts: Chart.js

Data storage: localStorage (can be extended to Mavo or a real API)

Animations: CSS keyframes (flow-pulse, flow-move)

Bottom Line
This project transforms static remittance numbers into an interactive, geographic story — helping anyone from government analysts to journalists see where money flows from, how much, and whether it’s growing — all in a self-contained, no-backend web app.
